intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls selling yakitori and dango, and soak in the festive atmosphere. The park is illuminated at night creating a magical pink glow perfect for evening strolls with the family.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the famous Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, browse the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft stalls and snack vendors, and participate in omikuji fortune drawing. Kids love the vibrant atmosphere, traditional costumes for rent, and sampling ningyo-yaki (character-shaped cakes) along the way.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and historically essential experience for families. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the preserved Atomic Bomb Dome, and explore the museum which tells the story of August 6, 1945 in a respectful and educational way. Children can fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument, inspired by Sadako Sasaki's story. This experience fosters empathy, historical awareness, and meaningful family conversations.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture at the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and seasonal street snacks as you weave through vendor stalls. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to learn about Japanese culinary traditions, the art of sushi-making, and the history of the world's most famous fish market. A delicious and interactive cultural experience for all ages.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Explore the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Walk the towering bamboo path, visit the historic Tenryu-ji Zen garden with its stunning cherry blossom trees, and hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where Japanese macaques roam freely with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Kids absolutely love interacting with the monkeys, making this a perfect blend of nature, culture, and family fun.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Purchase a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for convenient transit use throughout the trip. Grab a quick convenience store meal at a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart inside the airport — onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods are excellent and very affordable.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or in transit
meals.dinner: Convenience store (7-Eleven / FamilyMart) at the airport — budget ¥500–¥800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Priority on arrival night: get to the hotel safely and rest. Buy your IC card at the airport vending machines — it will save time and money on every transit ride. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements since you arrive late at night.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag with a slow morning. Have a simple breakfast near the hotel. Walk around the local beachfront area of the resort to acclimate and enjoy the fresh morning air. Visit a nearby convenience store to stock up on snacks and drinks for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood around the resort. Visit a nearby shrine or local market to ease into Japanese culture. If energy allows, take a short local bus or train ride to the nearest town center to get oriented with public transportation and browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel. Visit a local izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant) for affordable shared dishes like karaage (fried chicken), edamame, and yakitori. Return early to rest ahead of the full itinerary starting tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or convenience store — budget ¥300–¥600
meals.lunch: Local ramen or udon shop near the resort — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the hotel — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day. Japan's public transit can be overwhelming at first — use this day to get comfortable with your IC card and local maps. Download Google Maps offline and the Japan Transit Planner app (Hyperdia or Navitime) for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early train to Tokyo and head straight to Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa. Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and stroll through Nakamise Shopping Street, lined with traditional snacks and souvenirs. Light incense at the temple and explore the temple grounds — entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Asakusa district on foot. Visit the nearby Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center (free observation deck on the 8th floor with great views). Walk along the Sumida River and cross to the other side for views of the Tokyo Skytree. Browse the Kappabashi Kitchen Street for fun kitchenware and plastic food replica shops — great for families.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno Park for an early evening cherry blossom stroll (late blooms may still be visible in mid-April). Grab street food from park vendors — yakitori skewers, taiyaki (fish-shaped cake), and corn on the cob. Return to the hotel via train using your IC card.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — budget ¥300–¥600
meals.lunch: Asakusa Menchikatsu (fried meat cutlet) from a Nakamise stall, plus matcha soft serve — budget ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Ueno park street food stalls or nearby yoshoku (Western-Japanese fusion) diner — budget ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji Temple is free to enter. Nakamise Shopping Street is great for budget souvenir shopping — ningyo-yaki (small cakes) make excellent affordable gifts. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 8–12 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto by Shinkansen (book in advance for best prices; consider a regional JR Pass if cost-effective for your group). Upon arrival at Kyoto Station, store luggage in coin lockers and head immediately to Maruyama Park for the famous Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. The iconic weeping cherry tree at the center of the park is a must-see — free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Maruyama Park to the nearby Yasaka Shrine (free entry) and then stroll through the beautiful Higashiyama district. Explore the preserved machiya (traditional townhouse) streets of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — photogenic stone-paved lanes lined with tea houses and craft shops. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 entry) perched on the hillside with stunning city views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in the Gion district — look for affordable set meals (teishoku) at local restaurants. Watch for geiko (Kyoto geisha) and maiko (apprentice geisha) walking to evening appointments around 17:30–18:30 near Hanamikoji Street. Return to your hotel or arrange overnight accommodation in Kyoto for convenience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departure — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine or obanzai (Kyoto-style small dishes) at a budget lunch spot near Higashiyama — budget ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal in Gion — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free and open 24 hours — it's especially magical at night with lantern lighting if cherry blossoms are still in season. Mid-April may see late cherry blossoms or fresh green leaves depending on the year. Book Shinkansen tickets in advance to save money. Kiyomizudera is one of Japan's most visited temples — arrive early to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha — the famous shrine with thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Entry is completely free and the lower trails are accessible for families. Hike as far as your group is comfortable — even 30–45 minutes up offers incredible scenery and fewer crowds than the base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short train ride to Arashiyama. Walk through the otherworldly Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (free to enter) — the towering bamboo creates a natural cathedral effect. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple garden (¥500) and stroll along the Oi River. Families can also visit the Arashiyama Monkey Park Iwatayama (¥600 per adult, ¥300 per child) for panoramic views of Kyoto and to see Japanese macaques up close.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed riverside dinner in Arashiyama before heading back to your accommodation. Try yudofu (hot tofu hot pot) — a Kyoto specialty that is warming, delicious, and very affordable.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store near accommodation — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Matcha soba noodles or tofu lunch near Arashiyama — budget ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yudofu restaurant in Arashiyama or convenience store bento on the train back — budget ¥800–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and best visited before 8:00 AM to avoid crowds — the upper trails are far less crowded and more atmospheric. The Bamboo Grove is a short walk from Arashiyama Station. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike — great for active families. Bring water and snacks from a convenience store to keep costs down.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Nijo Castle (¥1,030 entry) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former shogun residence in central Kyoto. The famous 'nightingale floors' that squeak when walked on were designed to detect intruders. The castle gardens are stunning in spring. Great for history-loving families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kyoto Imperial Palace and its surrounding Kyoto Gyoen National Garden (free entry). The garden is a beloved local park with open lawns, plum and cherry trees, and tranquil paths — perfect for a picnic lunch. Nearby, explore the Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') — a narrow covered market street with hundreds of food stalls selling pickles, grilled skewers, fresh tofu, and local delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train to Osaka (30 minutes from Kyoto on the Hankyu or JR line, very affordable). Explore the vibrant Dotonbori entertainment district along the canal — famous for its giant illuminated signs and street food culture. Try takoyaki (octopus balls) and okonomiyaki (savory pancakes) from street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market food stalls — budget ¥700–¥1,000 (mix of small bites)
meals.dinner: Dotonbori street food in Osaka — takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu — budget ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle is one of the best value historical sites in Kyoto. Nishiki Market is covered and walkable — great for rainy days. Osaka's Dotonbori is free to walk and the street food is world-class and very affordable. The Kyoto–Osaka train is inexpensive on the Hankyu line — use your IC card.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto/Osaka to Hiroshima by Shinkansen (approximately 45–90 minutes). Head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park. The museum (¥200 entry — extremely affordable) is one of the most important and moving historical experiences in Japan. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, visit the Atomic Bomb Dome (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and observe the Children's Peace Monument.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Peace Memorial Park at your own pace. Visit the Flame of Peace, the Peace Bell, and the Memorial Cenotaph. Take a short ferry ride (¥180 each way) to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (¥300 entry). Walk along the island's waterfront and encounter the famously tame deer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland and enjoy dinner in Hiroshima. Try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki — a layered savory pancake with noodles, different from the Osaka style and a local specialty. Return to accommodation in Hiroshima or travel back toward Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store before departure — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Miyajima street food — momiji manju (maple leaf cakes) and grilled oysters — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki at Okonomimura (a multi-floor building dedicated to okonomiyaki restaurants) — budget ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply moving and recommended for children aged 10 and up — discuss the history beforehand to prepare younger children. The museum entry fee of ¥200 is one of the best value cultural experiences in Japan. The Miyajima ferry is operated by JR (covered by JR Pass) or a private company. Check tide times — the floating torii gate looks best at high tide.

day_by_day.morning: Travel back toward the Tokyo area or explore a new region. If returning to Tokyo, use the Shinkansen and arrive by midday. Visit the Harajuku district — walk down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and affordable crepes. Nearby Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) is a serene forested sanctuary in the heart of the city — a beautiful contrast to the busy streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Harajuku through Yoyogi Park — a vast green space popular with families, musicians, and picnickers. If cherry blossoms are still visible, this is a wonderful spot for a relaxed hanami picnic. Continue to Shibuya to see the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection. Free to watch from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation area above.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shibuya's affordable dining options. Visit a conveyor belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) — budget-friendly and fun for families, with plates starting from ¥100–¥150 each. Alternatively, try a gyudon (beef bowl) chain like Yoshinoya or Sukiya for a filling meal under ¥500.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or Shinkansen ekiben (station bento box) — budget ¥500–¥900
meals.lunch: Crepe from Takeshita Street or picnic from convenience store in Yoyogi Park — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) in Shibuya — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free and one of Tokyo's most peaceful experiences — the forested path to the shrine is beautiful. Yoyogi Park is free and perfect for families. The Shibuya Scramble is best experienced at dusk when the lights are bright — go down into the crossing itself for the full effect. Gyudon chains are open 24 hours and extremely affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets in Tokyo (advance booking required, ¥3,200 per adult) — a world-renowned digital art museum that is spectacular for families and culture lovers. Alternatively, for a free option, visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (¥1,000 entry) — Japan's largest museum with an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, and historical artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akihabara — Tokyo's famous electronics and anime district. Browse multi-floor electronics stores, retro game shops, and manga cafes. Great for families interested in Japanese pop culture. Visit a maid cafe for a uniquely Japanese cultural experience (budget ¥500–¥1,000 for a drink and show). Walk to nearby Kanda Myojin Shrine (free) — a beautiful historic shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for dinner and evening exploration. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (open until 22:30) for panoramic night views of the entire city — completely free and one of Tokyo's best views. Explore the Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) alley in Shinjuku for tiny yakitori stalls with a nostalgic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen or curry restaurant — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori skewers and beer in Shinjuku — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab in advance online — tickets often sell out weeks ahead. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free and rivals paid observation decks — one of the best budget tips in Tokyo. Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) is atmospheric and authentic — tiny stalls, smoky grills, and cold beer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — visit the Tsukiji Outer Market (the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains open to the public). Enjoy a fresh sushi breakfast or try tamagoyaki (rolled omelette) and fresh seafood at market stalls. A quintessential Tokyo food experience at very reasonable prices. Browse the market shops for last-minute food souvenirs like dried seaweed, dashi, and Japanese snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon in the Ginza district — Tokyo's upscale shopping area. Window shopping is free and the architecture is beautiful. Visit the Itoya stationery store (a Tokyo institution) for beautiful and affordable Japanese paper goods and stationery as gifts. Head to the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond and teahouse, offering a peaceful final cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Japan — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal as a trip celebration. Try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant or a shabu-shabu (hot pot) restaurant with a budget set menu. Head to the airport early — allow at least 3 hours before departure. Use your remaining IC card balance on transit and spend any leftover small yen on airport snacks and duty-free souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market fresh sushi breakfast — budget ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Ginza department store basement food hall (depachika) — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu or shabu-shabu set menu near the airport or hotel — budget ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited before 10:00 AM when the freshest items are available. IC cards can be refunded at airport station machines before departure — keep your card if you plan to return to Japan. Pack any liquid food souvenirs (sauces, pickles) in checked luggage. Japan is extremely safe — leaving luggage in coin lockers at the station while you do final sightseeing is perfectly safe and convenient.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. In-flight or in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Land at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Use IC card (Suica/Pasmo) kiosks at the airport for convenient transit top-up. Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport transit food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a 24-hour convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the hotel — try onigiri, hot noodles, and Japanese milk bread for an authentic and affordable first taste of Japan.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag will be real. Lay out tomorrow's essentials before sleeping. Confirm hotel check-in accepts late arrivals. Exchange some yen at the airport or use an ATM at 7-Eleven (most reliable for foreign cards).

day_by_day.morning: Ease into Japan with a leisurely hotel breakfast, then take a short walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Explore the immediate neighborhood, find a local convenience store or bakery, and pick up a Japan Rail Pass or day pass if not already arranged. Spend the late morning visiting a nearby local shrine or coastal landmark to gently introduce the cultural atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest city center for orientation. Visit a local covered shopping arcade (shotengai) to browse traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Stop at a local tourist information center to collect maps and confirm upcoming transport logistics. If energy allows, visit a nearby garden or public park to enjoy the tail end of cherry blossom season.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first proper dinner at a mid-range izakaya (Japanese gastropub) near the hotel. Order a variety of small plates — edamame, yakitori, karaage, and miso soup — to sample Japanese comfort food in a lively, family-friendly atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Japanese staples like rice, miso soup, grilled fish, and tamagoyaki alongside Western options.
meals.lunch: Casual ramen or udon shop near the shopping arcade — budget ¥800–¥1,200 per person.
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the resort — budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule — jet lag from a long-haul flight typically peaks on Day 2. Confirm Day 3 travel arrangements to Kyoto or Tokyo this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for travel to Kyoto via Shinkansen (bullet train). Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning and check into a central guesthouse or leave luggage at the station. Head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Witness Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in full bloom surrounded by locals and families enjoying traditional flower-viewing picnics. The morning light is perfect for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Maruyama Park through the historic Higashiyama district along the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes. Browse traditional pottery, matcha sweets, and lacquerware shops. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched on a hillside with sweeping views over Kyoto's cityscape and cherry blossoms below. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full temple complex.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric Gion district at dusk — the traditional geisha quarter glows beautifully in the evening. Dine at a mid-range kaiseki-style restaurant or a tofu cuisine restaurant (Kyoto is famous for yudofu — hot tofu dishes). Return to your Kyoto accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab onigiri and green tea from a convenience store before the Shinkansen.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Maruyama Park — purchase bento boxes from Nishiki Market or a depachika (department store basement food hall) near Kyoto Station. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Tofu kaiseki restaurant in Gion or Higashiyama — try Okutan or a similar mid-range venue. Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom peak in Kyoto typically falls mid-to-late April — timing is ideal. Maruyama Park gets crowded on weekends; arrive before 9:00 AM for the best experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Higashiyama involves cobblestones and gentle hills.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or taxi to Arashiyama on the western outskirts of Kyoto. Walk through the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — the towering green stalks create an otherworldly corridor best experienced in the early morning before crowds arrive. Follow the path to Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning Zen garden with cherry blossoms reflected in the central pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bamboo grove, hike up to the Arashiyama Monkey Park (Iwatayama). The 20-minute uphill walk rewards families with panoramic views of Kyoto and the chance to hand-feed wild Japanese macaques. Children especially love this experience. Descend and explore Arashiyama's riverside promenade and browse craft shops along Togetsukyo Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — for an early evening food walk. Sample pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, skewered octopus balls, and sweet mochi. Dinner at a casual kaiseki or tempura restaurant near the Kawaramachi entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near Arashiyama Station — try morning set with toast, egg, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Riverside café or soba restaurant in Arashiyama — try cold zaru soba with dipping sauce. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Tempura teishoku (set meal) restaurant near Kawaramachi — crispy seasonal vegetables and seafood with rice and miso soup. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the bamboo grove by 7:30–8:00 AM to avoid peak crowds. The Monkey Park entrance fee is approximately ¥550 for adults and ¥250 for children. Bring cash — many Arashiyama vendors don't accept cards. The riverside is beautiful for family photos with cherry blossoms framing Togetsukyo Bridge.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to Kyoto's golden cultural corridor. Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — the iconic Zen temple whose gold-leaf exterior shimmers over a mirror pond. Arrive early to beat tour groups. Nearby, explore Ryoan-ji Temple's world-famous rock garden, one of the finest examples of karesansui (dry landscape) design. Both are within 15 minutes of each other.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nijo Castle — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former shogun palace. Walk the 'nightingale floors' that chirp underfoot to alert guards of intruders. The castle grounds burst with cherry blossoms in April, making it one of Kyoto's best blossom spots. Explore the ornate painted interiors of the Ninomaru Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Japanese tea ceremony experience at a local teahouse in Kyoto (many offer 45–60 minute sessions for ¥2,000–¥3,500). Afterward, dinner at a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant where you cook thin slices of wagyu beef in a communal pot at the table — a fun, interactive family dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a fresh matcha latte and wagashi (traditional sweet) from a Kinkaku-ji area café.
meals.lunch: Obanzai (Kyoto-style home cooking) set lunch at a local restaurant near Nijo Castle — seasonal vegetables, pickles, rice, and miso soup. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu restaurant in central Kyoto — mid-range course sets typically run ¥3,500–¥6,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a combined temple/castle day pass if available for savings. Kinkaku-ji is best photographed in the morning with calm reflective water. The tea ceremony can be booked in advance online — En tea ceremony and Urasenke are reputable options. This is a full cultural day — pace it with breaks for children.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto to Tokyo via Shinkansen (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi). Arrive in Tokyo late morning. Check in or drop luggage at your Tokyo accommodation. Head straight to Asakusa district to visit Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most beloved Buddhist temple, dating to 628 AD. Enter through the dramatic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) with its enormous red lantern.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the full length of Nakamise Shopping Street leading to Senso-ji's main hall — browse traditional Japanese souvenirs, ningyo-yaki cakes, fans, and kokeshi dolls. Great for picking up gifts. Explore the temple grounds, the five-story pagoda, and the surrounding Asakusa backstreets with their old-Tokyo (shitamachi) atmosphere. Visit the nearby Sumida Park for lingering cherry blossom views along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Tokyo Skytree visit (Japan's tallest tower, adjacent to Asakusa) for breathtaking city views at sunset and into the evening. Dine in the Skytree's restaurant floor or head back to Asakusa for dinner at a traditional tempura or unagi (eel) restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Shinkansen ekiben (station bento box) at Kyoto Station — a beloved Japanese travel tradition. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Ningyo-yaki and street snacks along Nakamise, plus a sit-down lunch at a soba restaurant in Asakusa. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Unagi (grilled eel over rice) restaurant in Asakusa — a Tokyo specialty. Mid-range sets ¥2,500–¥4,500.

day_by_day.notes: The Shinkansen from Kyoto to Tokyo runs frequently — book reserved seats in advance, especially on a Tuesday when business travelers fill trains. Senso-ji is one of Japan's most visited sites — early afternoon on a weekday is manageable. Tokyo Skytree tickets can be purchased online to skip queues (¥2,100 for the first observation deck).

day_by_day.morning: Start with the world-famous Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 8:00 AM to catch the freshest action. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled egg), tuna sashimi, grilled scallops, and Japanese pickles from vendor stalls. This is one of the most exciting food experiences in all of Japan and perfect for adventurous families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional garden with a tidal pond, teahouse, and seasonal flowers, located right next to the market. Take a water bus from Hamarikyu along the Sumida River back toward Asakusa for a scenic Tokyo waterway perspective. Spend the late afternoon exploring Akihabara (Electric Town) — fascinating for kids with its anime, gaming arcades, and electronics.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the vibrant Shibuya or Shinjuku district. Experience the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection. Dine at a conveyor-belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant for a fun, affordable, and delicious family meal.

meals.breakfast: The Tsukiji Outer Market IS breakfast — graze on fresh sushi, tamago, and seafood skewers. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person for a full market crawl.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse — matcha and wagashi in a serene traditional setting. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) in Shibuya — Sushiro or Kurazushi chains offer excellent quality at ¥150–¥300 per plate. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open to the public daily (most vendors open 5:00 AM–2:00 PM). The inner wholesale market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains a must-visit food destination. Hamarikyu water bus tickets are approximately ¥780 per adult. Akihabara arcades are free to enter — bring yen coins for games.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Tokyo to Hiroshima via Shinkansen (approximately 4 hours — depart early). Arrive mid-morning. Head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and historically essential experience. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), and spend time in the museum learning about August 6, 1945 and the path to peace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Peace Park — visit the Children's Peace Monument (Sadako's statue surrounded by thousands of paper cranes), the Flame of Peace, and the Memorial Cenotaph. Cross the bridge to explore Hiroshima Castle — a reconstructed feudal castle with an excellent history museum inside. The castle grounds offer cherry blossom views in April.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hiroshima's beloved local specialty — Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake with noodles, cabbage, and pork). Head to Okonomi-mura ('Okonomiyaki Village') — a multi-story building packed with small okonomiyaki restaurants where you watch the chef cook your meal right in front of you on a teppan griddle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab an early bento at Tokyo Station before boarding the Shinkansen.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Peace Park café or a nearby restaurant — try Hiroshima-style ramen (rich soy-based broth). Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Hiroshima okonomiyaki at Okonomi-mura — a full meal with layers of flavor. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person. Pair with local Hiroshima sake or Calpis soda for the kids.

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional — prepare children in age-appropriate ways beforehand. Allow at least 2 hours for the museum. Photography is permitted in the park but be respectful near memorials. Consider staying overnight in Hiroshima to reduce travel fatigue, or return to Tokyo in the evening if preferred. The museum charges ¥200 admission — one of the most affordable and important museums in the world.

day_by_day.morning: Take a 25-minute ferry from Hiroshima (or Miyajimaguchi) to Miyajima Island — one of Japan's three most scenic views. Visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine with its famous 'floating' torii gate rising from the sea. Explore the shrine buildings built over the water, and walk the forested island paths. Wild deer roam freely around the island and are friendly with visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up Mt. Misen via ropeway for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea and surrounding islands. Descend and explore Miyajima's Omotesando shopping street — try momiji manju (maple-leaf-shaped cakes filled with red bean paste), the island's most famous souvenir and snack. Return by ferry to the mainland and travel back toward your base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo or your hotel base. If time allows, enjoy a final evening stroll through a local shopping district or night market. Relax with a traditional Japanese onsen (hot spring bath) experience — many mid-range hotels and public sento bathhouses offer this. A perfect way to soothe tired legs after 9 days of walking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near the ferry terminal.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on Miyajima Island — grilled oysters (Hiroshima oysters are world-famous) and anago (conger eel) rice box. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Casual ramen or Japanese curry restaurant near your hotel — a comforting and affordable final-night-away meal. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.

day_by_day.notes: The Itsukushima torii gate is most dramatic at high tide when it appears to float — check tide tables before visiting. Miyajima ropeway costs approximately ¥1,000 one-way per adult. The deer are wild — do not feed them paper or plastic. Miyajima is also strikingly beautiful at night if you can stay for sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan. Return to your hotel base and enjoy a leisurely final Japanese breakfast. Pack and prepare for departure. If time allows before checkout, take a short walk to a nearby park or shrine for one last peaceful moment in Japan. Visit a local 100-yen shop (Daiso) or department store for any last-minute gifts or forgotten souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with ample time — allow at least 3 hours before international departure. At the airport, browse the duty-free shops for Japanese whisky, Kit-Kat flavors (Japan has dozens of unique varieties), cosmetics, and packaged wagashi sweets. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at one of the airport's excellent terminal restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days — cherry blossoms in Maruyama Park, the bamboo groves of Arashiyama, the solemnity of Hiroshima, the flavors of Tsukiji, and the timeless temples of Kyoto and Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the miso soup, grilled fish, and rice one last time.
meals.lunch: Airport terminal restaurant — try a katsu curry, ramen, or sushi set for a satisfying final Japanese meal. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport lounge if applicable.

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card (Suica/Pasmo) at the airport for a refund of remaining balance minus a ¥220 handling fee — or keep it as a reusable souvenir for your next Japan trip. Confirm your flight check-in time and terminal in advance. Japan's airports are highly efficient — security and boarding are smooth, but international departures still require early arrival. Carry any liquids, fresh food, or fresh produce purchased at the market in checked luggage per customs regulations.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls selling yakitori and dango, and soak in the festive atmosphere. The park is illuminated at night creating a magical pink glow perfect for evening strolls with the family.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the famous Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, browse the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft stalls and snack vendors, and participate in omikuji fortune drawing. Kids love the vibrant atmosphere, traditional costumes for rent, and sampling ningyo-yaki (character-shaped cakes) along the way.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and historically essential experience for families. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the preserved Atomic Bomb Dome, and explore the museum which tells the story of August 6, 1945 in a respectful and educational way. Children can fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument, inspired by Sadako Sasaki's story. This experience fosters empathy, historical awareness, and meaningful family conversations.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture at the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and seasonal street snacks as you weave through vendor stalls. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to learn about Japanese culinary traditions, the art of sushi-making, and the history of the world's most famous fish market. A delicious and interactive cultural experience for all ages.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Explore the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Walk the towering bamboo path, visit the historic Tenryu-ji Zen garden with its stunning cherry blossom trees, and hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where Japanese macaques roam freely with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Kids absolutely love interacting with the monkeys, making this a perfect blend of nature, culture, and family fun.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tokyo Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged limousine or premium taxi) will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and unwind in your beachfront suite. Light welcome amenities and room service available.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — request the Japanese kaiseki tasting box or premium wagyu onigiri set available after hours

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the resort concierge. Request early check-in preparation so the room is fully ready upon late arrival. Stock the minibar with preferred beverages ahead of time. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 23:30 local time to begin adjusting to Japan Standard Time.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start to recover from jet lag. Enjoy a lavish Japanese-Western fusion breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront property, breathing in the sea air and acclimating to the local time zone. Explore the resort's spa facilities — book a traditional Japanese onsen soak or shiatsu massage to ease travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation excursion: Take a private guided tour of the surrounding local area near the resort. Visit a nearby Shinto shrine for a gentle cultural introduction — participate in a purification ritual (temizuya hand-washing) and receive an omamori (good luck charm). Browse a local artisan market for handcrafted Japanese souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's beachfront terrace, watching the Pacific horizon glow. Enjoy a formal multi-course kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, featuring seasonal spring ingredients and local seafood paired with premium sake selections.

meals.breakfast: Resort oceanfront restaurant — Japanese-Western fusion buffet with fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, wagyu beef, pastries, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled seafood bento and chilled matcha
meals.dinner: Resort kaiseki restaurant — 10-course seasonal tasting menu featuring sakura-themed spring dishes, paired with curated sake flight

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to combat jet lag. Encourage the family to nap briefly in the afternoon if needed but aim to stay on local time by evening. Book the spa and dinner reservations through the concierge upon check-in the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Tokyo (approximately 1–2 hours depending on resort location). Begin the day at Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple dating to 628 AD. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to experience the temple before crowds swell. A private guide will explain the history of the Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, the five-story pagoda, and the main hall. Draw an omikuji fortune slip as a family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Nakamise Shopping Street, the historic 250-meter arcade leading to Senso-ji, lined with traditional craft shops and snack stalls. Shop for premium wagashi (Japanese sweets), fans, lacquerware, and silk goods. Afterward, transfer to the Tsukiji Outer Market for a private premium food tour — sample fresh uni, otoro sushi, tamagoyaki, and seasonal street foods with an expert culinary guide.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Ginza district for an evening of luxury shopping and dining. Visit the flagship Itoya stationery store and premium Japanese boutiques. Dinner at a celebrated Ginza sushi omakase restaurant — chef's counter experience with 18–20 courses of Edomae-style nigiri.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a traditional Japanese morning set (teishoku) at a renowned Asakusa café near Senso-ji
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market premium food tour — curated tastings of sushi, sashimi, tamagoyaki, fresh fruit, and seafood skewers
meals.dinner: Ginza omakase sushi restaurant (e.g., Sushi Saito-style establishment) — 18-course Edomae nigiri with premium sake pairings

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Hire a licensed English-speaking guide for the temple and Nakamise portion. The Tsukiji food tour should be pre-booked with a premium culinary tour company. Confirm omakase reservation weeks in advance as top Tokyo sushi counters book out quickly. Private car and driver recommended for the full Tokyo day.

day_by_day.morning: Board a reserved-seat Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — a scenic 2.5-hour journey through the Japanese countryside, with views of Mount Fuji on clear spring days. Arrive in Kyoto and transfer by private car to Maruyama Park for the quintessential cherry blossom viewing experience (hanami). The park's iconic 100-year-old weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) should be in full or late bloom in mid-April. Enjoy a private hanami picnic setup arranged by your guide under the blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Gion, Kyoto's legendary geisha district, with a knowledgeable guide explaining the ochaya (teahouse) culture, machiya townhouses, and the arts of the geiko and maiko. Visit Yasaka Shrine adjacent to Maruyama Park. In the late afternoon, explore Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — preserved stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops selling Kiyomizu pottery, bamboo crafts, and matcha confections.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private kaiseki dinner at a renowned Kyoto ryotei (traditional restaurant) in Gion, featuring Kyoto-style kyo-ryori cuisine. Optional: arrange a private maiko (apprentice geisha) performance and tea ceremony experience during dinner for the family — a rare and unforgettable cultural highlight.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen bento (ekiben) — purchase a premium regional bento at Tokyo Station before boarding
meals.lunch: Private hanami picnic in Maruyama Park — curated bento boxes with seasonal Kyoto delicacies, matcha, and sakura mochi prepared by a local caterer
meals.dinner: Kyoto ryotei kaiseki dinner in Gion — 12-course kyo-ryori with optional maiko entertainment; sake and premium Japanese whisky pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom timing in mid-April may feature late blooms or falling petals (hanafubuki — cherry blossom snowfall), which is considered equally beautiful. Confirm Shinkansen reservations in advance via JR Pass or direct booking. The maiko dinner experience must be arranged weeks ahead through a specialized cultural concierge service. Stay overnight at a luxury Kyoto hotel or ryokan (recommend Tawaraya or The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — arrive before 8:00 AM to experience the ethereal green cathedral of towering bamboo in near-solitude before day-trippers arrive. A private guide will lead the family through the grove, explaining the cultural and ecological significance. Afterward, visit Tenryu-ji Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Zen garden with stunning pond reflections and spring foliage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the scenic Sagano Romantic Train (Torokko Train) through the Hozugawa River gorge — a charming family-friendly rail journey through forested mountains and cherry blossom trees. Disembark and enjoy a traditional boat ride down the Hozu River rapids back toward Arashiyama. Visit the Iwatayama Monkey Park — hike a short trail to meet over 120 free-roaming Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto below.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto for a relaxing evening. Visit the Nishiki Market (Kyoto's Kitchen) for premium food browsing and tastings. Dinner at a celebrated Kyoto teppanyaki restaurant featuring A5 Kobe/Wagyu beef prepared tableside by a master chef.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan or hotel traditional Japanese breakfast — miso soup, grilled fish, pickles, rice, tofu, and tamagoyaki
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch in Arashiyama at Yoshida-ya or similar premium restaurant — kaiseki bento overlooking the Oi River with tofu cuisine
meals.dinner: Kyoto teppanyaki restaurant — A5 Wagyu beef, seasonal vegetables, and seafood prepared tableside; premium Japanese whisky or sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Torokko Train and Hozu River boat ride are family favorites and should be reserved in advance, especially during spring season. The Monkey Park involves a 15-minute uphill hike — comfortable walking shoes essential. Nishiki Market closes around 18:00, so plan accordingly. Consider a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through Arashiyama for a luxurious and fun family experience.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive cultural morning: Private tea ceremony workshop at an authentic Kyoto machiya (traditional townhouse) with a tea master. The family learns the philosophy and precise choreography of chado (the way of tea), dresses in kimono for the experience, and participates in a full ura-senke style ceremony. Followed by a private Ikebana (Japanese flower arranging) class using spring cherry blossoms and seasonal blooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle — the opulent 17th-century shogun palace with famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp when walked upon (a security feature against ninja intruders). Explore the Ninomaru Palace's stunning painted screens and ornate interiors with a private guide. Stroll the castle's cherry blossom garden. Then visit Kinkaku-ji (the Golden Pavilion) — Kyoto's most iconic temple, its gold-leaf facade shimmering over a mirror-like pond.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll through the Philosopher's Path — a 2km canal-side walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees in late bloom. Evening dinner at a premium Kyoto restaurant specializing in yudofu (tofu hot pot) and obanzai (Kyoto-style small plates), reflecting the city's refined Buddhist culinary tradition.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or ryokan breakfast — traditional Japanese set with seasonal miso, grilled mackerel, and house-made pickles
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch near Nijo Castle — kaiseki bento at a renowned Kyoto restaurant featuring seasonal bamboo shoots, cherry blossom-cured fish, and spring vegetables
meals.dinner: Kyoto obanzai restaurant near Philosopher's Path — yudofu hot pot, seasonal small plates, and local Fushimi sake

day_by_day.notes: Kimono rental and dressing assistance can be arranged through the tea ceremony venue or a specialist kimono shop. Kinkaku-ji is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin. The Philosopher's Path is especially magical at dusk when lanterns along the canal begin to glow. Book all cultural workshops well in advance through a Kyoto cultural concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima via Shinkansen (approximately 1.5 hours from Kyoto). Arrive and proceed directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park — a profoundly moving and historically essential experience for the family. A private guide will lead a respectful and age-appropriate tour through the museum's powerful exhibits documenting the 1945 atomic bombing and Japan's journey toward peace. Pay respects at the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Peace Memorial Park — visit the Children's Peace Monument (inspired by Sadako Sasaki) and fold origami paper cranes as a family tribute. Cross the Motoyasu River to explore Hiroshima's revitalized city center. Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island — home to the iconic 'floating' Otorii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (another UNESCO site). Explore the shrine, feed the friendly deer roaming the island, and climb the hillside for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Hiroshima city featuring the region's signature dish — Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake with noodles and local oysters) at a premium establishment. Return to Kyoto by Shinkansen.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or premium Shinkansen ekiben from Kyoto Station
meals.lunch: Miyajima Island lunch — fresh grilled Hiroshima oysters, momiji manju (maple-leaf cakes), and seasonal seafood at a waterfront restaurant
meals.dinner: Premium Hiroshima okonomiyaki restaurant — chef's table experience with layered okonomiyaki, local Seto Inland Sea oysters, and Hiroshima Tomoé sake

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. The museum is closed on certain Mondays; verify hours in advance. Miyajima's floating torii gate appearance depends on tidal timing — check tide charts and aim for high tide in the afternoon for the iconic 'floating' effect. Ferry to Miyajima is covered by JR Pass. This is a long but deeply rewarding day.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo via Shinkansen (2.5 hours). Check into a luxury Tokyo hotel (e.g., The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). Morning visit to the Imperial Palace East Gardens — the former innermost citadel of Edo Castle, featuring manicured traditional gardens, stone walls, and seasonal blooms. A private guide narrates the history of the Tokugawa shogunate and imperial legacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park — Tokyo's cultural heartland. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's oldest and largest museum) with a private curator-led tour of its world-class collection of samurai armor, ancient pottery, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Afterward, stroll through Ueno Park's cherry tree lanes (late blooms or green canopy by this date) and visit Ueno Zoo for younger family members.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Tokyo from above: cocktails at the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (famous from 'Lost in Translation') on the 52nd floor with panoramic night skyline views. Dinner at a celebrated Tokyo French-Japanese fusion restaurant in Shinjuku or Marunouchi.

meals.breakfast: Premium Shinkansen ekiben or hotel breakfast upon Tokyo arrival
meals.lunch: Ueno area lunch — refined bento at a museum restaurant or traditional Japanese restaurant near the park featuring seasonal spring cuisine
meals.dinner: Tokyo French-Japanese fusion restaurant (e.g., Joel Robuchon Tokyo or similar) — tasting menu with Japanese ingredients interpreted through French technique; wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum requires advance booking for private guided tours. New York Bar at Park Hyatt has a cover charge in the evenings — reservations recommended. Consider a helicopter or rooftop experience for dramatic Tokyo skyline views if budget allows. Confirm hotel concierge has all remaining reservations confirmed.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Tokyo family adventure begins in Harajuku: Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, offering a peaceful contrast to Tokyo's urban energy. Participate in a traditional o-mairi shrine visit ritual. Walk the forested approach path (1.7km of towering cypress trees). Then explore Omotesando — Tokyo's most elegant boulevard — for luxury shopping at flagship stores (Louis Vuitton, Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons) and Japanese designer boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Odaiba for family-friendly premium experiences: Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets — the world-renowned immersive digital art museum where art and technology merge into breathtaking interactive environments that children and adults alike find magical. Explore the futuristic waterfront with views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay. Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) featuring ASIMO robots and space exploration exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell family dinner at a world-class Tokyo restaurant: reserve a table at a celebrated tempura kappo restaurant or a premium shabu-shabu establishment where A5 Wagyu is cooked at the table. End the evening with a nighttime cruise on Tokyo Bay — a private boat charter with champagne and skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel luxury breakfast — Japanese or Western selection with fresh-pressed juices, artisan coffee, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Omotesando area lunch — premium café or brasserie in one of the designer complex restaurants (e.g., Omotesando Hills dining floor)
meals.dinner: Tokyo premium shabu-shabu or tempura kappo restaurant — A5 Wagyu and seasonal seafood; followed by private Tokyo Bay night cruise with champagne

day_by_day.notes: teamLab museums require advance ticket booking — they sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. The private Tokyo Bay cruise should be arranged through the hotel concierge. Meiji Shrine is free to enter. Omotesando shopping budget should be planned in advance. This is an ideal penultimate day balancing culture, technology, and family fun.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Tokyo. Enjoy a long, indulgent hotel breakfast. Last-minute luxury shopping in Ginza — visit the Itoya flagship stationery store, Mikimoto pearls, and Higashiya confectionery for premium Japanese gifts and souvenirs. Stop at a renowned wagashi (Japanese sweet) shop to bring home seasonal sakura confections and premium matcha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills for a final cultural experience with sweeping Tokyo views from the observation deck. Alternatively, enjoy a final matcha ceremony and light lunch at a Ginza tea salon. Private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport — allow 2–3 hours before departure. Utilize premium airport lounge facilities for a relaxed pre-flight experience.
day_by_day.evening: Board departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Japan's cherry blossoms, ancient temples, moving history, and vibrant culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel luxury breakfast — order à la carte favorites; savor the last Japanese breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Ginza premium lunch — seasonal kaiseki or soba at a celebrated Ginza restaurant; or airport lounge dining if time is tight
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium cabin meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all luggage is packed the night before. Use the hotel's luggage forwarding service (takuhaibin) to send heavy bags directly to the airport if needed — a quintessentially convenient Japanese service. Collect any tax refunds at the airport's duty-free counters. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. The hotel concierge should arrange the private airport transfer the evening before. Sayonara — and arigato gozaimashita!
